question: Can an LLM generate safer and more effective repairs than RulesPlus on independent Korean retrieval failures under the same observations and tool budget?
data_scope: Small new-domain attributed source adaptations; authored queries, not real-user logs. Provisional labels require independent review. No final evaluation before both arms are frozen and paid approval is obtained.
evidence_guard: Every term must be a literal query/document span in the common context; no morphology-only semantic veto. Literal support is not proof of semantic equivalence. Full regression gate is evaluator-only.
evaluation: All candidates for all queries and both arms frozen before any label scoring; fixed query order; independent cumulative sandbox per arm; rejected patches discarded; no verdict returned to candidate process.
success: At least 20 independent reviewed concept groups, positive lower 95% group-bootstrap bound on failed-query final nDCG difference LLM minus rules, no healthy metric drop over 0.02 and no greater healthy regression fraction than rules, within approved budget. Otherwise superiority is withheld; report negative/descriptive outcomes.

llm.pricing: must freeze selected model/current official prices and exact pilot call cap after separate approval; model not auto substituted

future_protocol_changes: new_version_before_outcomes; never overwrite prior protocol or results
